title: What the Company Does: Segments, Revenue Mix & Concrete Real-World Customer Examples
book_title: Inside the Confidence Platform: Three Suites, One Control Plane

epigraph.quote: In enterprise software, backup gets you in the door, governance keeps you in the budget, and migration makes switching away too painful to contemplate.
epigraph.author: Cloud Infrastructure Analyst Note

web_blocks.html: AvePoint runs one unified SaaS architecture: the AvePoint Confidence Platform. It protects, governs, and modernizes unstructured enterprise data across Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, Salesforce, AWS, Azure, and multi-cloud estates [7, 8]. Financially, AvePoint reports revenue across four accounting lines [2]. In FY2025, SaaS generated $319.2M (76.1% of revenue), Services $53.8M (12.8%), Term License and Support $41.4M (9.9%), and Maintenance $5.1M (1.2%) [2]. Commercially, management organizes Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR) into three product suites: Resilience (~62% of ARR), Control (~26% of ARR), and Modernization (~12% of ARR) [7].

web_blocks.takeaway: Nearly two-thirds of ARR is anchored in mission-critical backup and resilience, while the faster-growing Control Suite (~26% of ARR) captures enterprise urgency around AI data governance and oversharing.

web_blocks.html: 1. Resilience Suite (~62% of ARR): The Resilience Suite is AvePoint's cash-generating anchor, led by AvePoint Cloud Backup and AvePoint Opus [7, 8]. Native Microsoft 365 retention policies do not provide air-gapped, immutable backups. If an admin account is breached or a Teams channel is purged, native recovery windows expire quickly. Concrete Real-World Example: A major Midwestern University Academic Healthcare System supports roughly 45,000 employees and partner hospitals [10]. It faced severe HIPAA risk from unmanaged Microsoft Teams and SharePoint sprawl overseen by just six IT staffers. The health system deployed AvePoint Cloud Backup and Cloud Governance to protect over 45 terabytes of Microsoft 365 data [10]. Priced on a per-user and capacity subscription, the platform automated workspace renewals, protected HIPAA records, and cut IT helpdesk tickets by 20% [10]. Once 45+ terabytes of regulated clinical snapshots sit in AvePoint's vault, switching costs rise sharply [10].

2. Control Suite (~26% of ARR): The Control Suite spans Cloud Governance, Policies & Insights, EnPower, and AgentPulse for AI agent oversight [7, 8]. It solves the biggest blocker to enterprise AI rollout: data oversharing. When a user queries Microsoft 365 Copilot, the AI surfaces any file that user can view, including misconfigured HR or executive folders. Concrete Real-World Example: Gonzaga University is a private Jesuit university with an open academic culture [11]. It struggled with anonymous sharing links and orphaned workspaces left by graduating students and departing faculty. Rather than keeping complex legacy tools like Varonis, Gonzaga deployed AvePoint's governance and risk tools [11]. Priced per active user seat under an annual SaaS contract, AvePoint automated permission recertification and centralized risk visibility without adding IT headcount [11]. The deployment gave Gonzaga's security team continuous oversight across SharePoint and Teams without slowing academic collaboration [11].

3. Modernization Suite (~12% of ARR) & MSP Delivery: This suite includes Fly (tenant-to-tenant migration), tyGraph (Copilot adoption analytics, acquired in 2022), and AvePoint Elements (the multi-tenant MSP console) [7, 9, 15]. Concrete Real-World Example: Dutch Managed Service Provider MostWare needed to standardize Microsoft 365 migrations and security baselines across dozens of SMB clients [12]. Manual PowerShell scripts ate up hours each month. MostWare adopted AvePoint Elements with multi-tenant Cloud Backup and Policies & Insights, billed on a monthly seat-and-consumption basis [12]. Migration times dropped by up to 80%. MostWare also automated monthly risk audits and turned one-off projects into sticky monthly recurring revenue (MRR) security contracts [12]. Today, Elements lets MSPs scale managed compliance without adding administrative headcount [9, 12].

web_blocks.title: Geographic & Vertical Diversification
paragraphs: AvePoint is unusually balanced geographically for a US-listed mid-cap software firm [6]. In FY2024, North America generated 41.1% of GAAP revenue ($135.9M), EMEA 30.0% ($99.3M), and APAC 28.9% ($95.4M) [6]. Public sector, healthcare, financial services, and higher education form its core regulated verticals. Strict compliance mandates like FedRAMP, GDPR, and UK G-Cloud create a procurement barrier against smaller startups [10, 11].

All three suites reinforce one another across IT spending cycles. Migration projects via Fly and tyGraph bring new enterprise tenants onto the platform [7, 15]. Ransomware risk anchors multi-year Resilience renewals [8, 10]. Generative AI rollouts then trigger high-margin Control seat expansions [7, 8]. Because all three suites share one data model, each added module lowers switching risk and lifts customer lifetime value [7, 8]. Pricing scales per active user seat and protected storage capacity, aligning AvePoint's revenue with enterprise data growth [8, 10].

book_paragraphs: If you ask a casual observer what AvePoint does, they will usually say 'Microsoft 365 backup.' That answer is roughly 62% right—and 38% dangerously incomplete. When you look under the hood of the AvePoint Confidence Platform, you find three interlocking product suites sharing a single cloud control plane, each solving a different stage of an enterprise's data lifecycle. Together, they explain why AvePoint has been able to expand inside existing accounts at a 112% Net Retention Rate even when IT budgets are under scrutiny.

book_subsections.title: The Resilience Suite (~62% of ARR): Backup as the Budget Wedge
paragraphs: Start with the Resilience Suite, which represents roughly 62% of AvePoint's Annual Recurring Revenue. Most executives assume that because Microsoft hosts Exchange, SharePoint, and Teams in the cloud, Microsoft is backing up their data forever. In reality, Microsoft guarantees infrastructure uptime, not long-term, air-gapped, item-level recovery from ransomware, malicious insider deletion, or misconfigured retention rules. Once a native recycle bin window expires, that data is gone.

Consider a real-world deployment at a major Midwestern University Academic Healthcare System supporting 45,000 employees and partner hospitals. Their IT team had only six people trying to police a 'wild west' sprawl of Microsoft Teams and SharePoint sites containing HIPAA-regulated patient and operational records. They deployed AvePoint Cloud Backup alongside Cloud Governance on an annual per-user and capacity subscription, protecting over 45 terabytes of data. Not only did they secure immutable recovery for HIPAA compliance, they automated workspace ownership renewals and cut IT helpdesk tickets by 20%. Once 45 terabytes of historical snapshots sit inside AvePoint's vault, switching costs become enormous.

book_subsections.title: The Control Suite (~26% of ARR): Turning AI Anxiety into Recurring Revenue
paragraphs: If backup is the wedge, the Control Suite—at roughly 26% of ARR—is the expansion engine. Generative AI tools like Microsoft 365 Copilot changed enterprise security overnight. Before AI, an overly permissive SharePoint folder or an anonymous sharing link sat unnoticed unless someone stumbled across it. With Copilot, any employee can type a natural-language prompt and instantly surface sensitive salary files, legal drafts, or M&A memos they technically had permission to view.

Look at Gonzaga University. With thousands of students, faculty, and staff collaborating openly, Gonzaga suffered from anonymous external links and orphaned workspaces left behind by graduating classes. Instead of maintaining heavy, fragmented legacy tools like Varonis, Gonzaga deployed AvePoint's governance and risk management suite—priced per active user seat—to continuously scan permissions, quarantine overshared files, and automate access recertification. Today, AvePoint has extended that same Control Suite into AgentPulse to govern autonomous AI agents, giving CIOs and CISOs a single dashboard for data hygiene.

book_subsections.title: The Modernization Suite (~12% of ARR) and Global Vertical Balance
paragraphs: The remaining 12% of ARR sits in the Modernization Suite—products like Fly for high-speed tenant-to-tenant migrations, tyGraph for Microsoft 365 and Copilot adoption telemetry, and AvePoint Elements for Managed Service Providers. Watch how a Dutch MSP like MostWare uses Elements: previously, migrating clients into Microsoft 365 and auditing security settings required hours of manual PowerShell scripting every month. By deploying Elements on a monthly consumption basis, MostWare cut migration times by up to 80% and turned one-off IT projects into recurring monthly managed-security contracts.

Equally striking is AvePoint's geographic and vertical balance. Unlike US-centric SaaS peers that generate 80% of revenue domestically, AvePoint's FY2024 GAAP revenue was split 41.1% North America, 30.0% EMEA, and 28.9% APAC, with deep penetration in regulated public sector, healthcare, financial services, and higher education accounts.

Why does that vertical mix matter to you and me as fundamental analysts? Because regulated buyers—federal agencies, hospital networks, universities, and banks—do not rip out compliance infrastructure to save 10% on a renewal. They require FedRAMP authorization, strict GDPR data residency, and immutable audit trails that small point-solution startups cannot afford to certify. That is also why Services revenue ($53.8 million, or 12.8% of FY2025 revenue) remains a strategic asset rather than a drag: complex tenant-to-tenant M&A consolidations and legacy archive migrations often start as services-assisted Fly engagements and convert into multi-year Resilience and Control SaaS subscriptions.

Look at the accounting mix shift as a final confirmation of how the platform is landing. In FY2021, SaaS was 44.6% of revenue. By FY2025, SaaS reached $319.2 million, or 76.1% of the $419.5 million total, while Term License and Support dropped to 9.9% ($41.4 million) and legacy Maintenance shrank to just 1.2% ($5.1 million). By Q3 2026, SaaS hit 80.5% of total revenue ($105.5 million out of $131.1 million). You are looking at a business whose legacy drag is virtually gone, leaving a pure multi-suite cloud compounding engine.

Equally important is how pricing aligns with customer growth across all three suites. In Resilience, AvePoint prices on a per-user seat and storage-capacity basis, meaning backup ARR expands organically as employee headcount and unstructured SharePoint/Teams data volumes grow. In Control, pricing scales per active seat across governance and AI-readiness modules, capturing higher average revenue per user whenever an enterprise activates Microsoft 365 Copilot or autonomous agents. And in Modernization, migration projects via Fly and analytics via tyGraph create natural entry points that convert into recurring platform subscriptions.

book_subsections.title: Why Three Suites Beat Three Point Vendors
paragraphs: To appreciate the commercial power of the Confidence Platform, put yourself in the seat of a Chief Information Officer at a 10,000-employee enterprise. You have three urgent problems: you just acquired a subsidiary whose Google Workspace and SharePoint data must be merged into your primary Microsoft 365 tenant; your CISO demands air-gapped, immutable backups so ransomware cannot encrypt your Teams and Exchange history; and your CEO wants to roll out Microsoft 365 Copilot next quarter without leaking confidential board or HR files.

Without AvePoint, you have to procure, integrate, and renew three separate vendors—one for migration, one for backup, and one for data security posture management. With AvePoint, your team runs Fly to migrate the data, turns on Cloud Backup and Opus to protect and tier cold storage, and activates Policies & Insights and Cloud Governance to lock down permissions before Copilot goes live. Every step feeds telemetry into the same control plane, lowering administrative overhead for the buyer and multiplying lifetime value for AvePoint.

Notice also how the three suites reinforce one another across different economic climates. During periods of corporate M&A or cloud-first IT modernization, Fly and tyGraph act as the tip of the spear, bringing new enterprise tenants onto the platform. During periods of heightened ransomware anxiety or regulatory tightening, Resilience—led by Cloud Backup and Opus—anchors multi-year renewals that CIOs treat as non-discretionary insurance. And during the current generative AI wave, Control—led by Cloud Governance, Policies & Insights, and AgentPulse—gives AvePoint a fresh seat-expansion catalyst inside accounts that already trust it with their backups. That three-legged stool is why AvePoint's revenue mix has proved resilient across both tight and expansionary IT spending cycles.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: Notice the architectural sequence here: Modernization gets the data into the cloud, Resilience backs it up and tiers cold storage, and Control governs who—and which AI agents—can touch it. Because all three suites share one underlying platform, each additional module sold into an existing tenant carries near-zero incremental onboarding friction.
